newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sees FCDUs hitting record $20 bln.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sees FCDUs hitting record $20 bln.

text.p: Foreign currency deposit units (FCDU) held by the Philippine commercial banking system are expected to reach a record level of $20 billion by the end of this year, the Central Bank said.
A Central Bank statement on Saturday said FCDU deposits as of last March 14 stood at $15.425 billion, an increase of $5.17 billion from the year-ago level of $10.25 billion.
"Given the rate of increase, the FCDU deposits could hit the $20 billion level by year-end," Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said.

Although not officially counted as part of the country's gross international reserves, FCDU deposits are considered a second layer of foreign reserves because most of these accounts are held by local exporters, officials say.
